_about: Introduced populations (the app's INVASIVE table / data-invasive) and whether published sources call each one invasive. status: 'invasive' only where a cited source says so; otherwise 'introduced'. Species pages use this for their wording; the app's own map table is unchanged.

python-bivittatus.text: Established in southern Florida, where its spread coincides with severe declines of medium-sized mammals in Everglades National Park.

src.title: Severe mammal declines coincide with proliferation of invasive Burmese pythons in Everglades National Park
src.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey (Dorcas et al., PNAS)

python-sebae.text: A small population was found in western Miami-Dade County; the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission considers it invasive and aims to eradicate it.

src.title: Northern African python: regulatory status
src.publisher: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

boiga-irregularis.text: Arrived on Guam shortly after the Second World War and caused the loss of most of the island's native forest birds.

src.title: Biology and impacts of Pacific island invasive species 2: Boiga irregularis, the brown tree snake

boa-constrictor.text: A naturalised population around Mayagüez, Puerto Rico, probably founded from the pet trade.

src.title: Genetic analysis of a novel invasion of Puerto Rico by an exotic constricting snake

boa-constrictor.text: First recorded on Aruba in 1999; a stable breeding population persists despite eradication efforts.

src.title: Genetic characterization of an invasive Boa constrictor population on the Caribbean island of Aruba

lampropeltis-californiae.text: Breeding in the wild on Gran Canaria since at least 2007; an EU LIFE project worked to control it because it eats the island's endemic lizards.

src.title: LIFE+ Lampropeltis: control of the invasive species Lampropeltis getula californiae on the island of Gran Canaria

pantherophis-guttatus.text: Established in the Cayman Islands and listed in the IUCN Global Invasive Species Database.

src.title: Elaphe guttata (Pantherophis guttatus)
src.publisher: IUCN SSC Invasive Species Specialist Group, Global Invasive Species Database

lycodon-capucinus.text: Introduced in the 1980s; experts consider it the most likely main cause of the collapse of Christmas Island's native lizards.

src.title: The lost lizards of Christmas Island: a retrospective assessment of factors driving the collapse of a native reptile community

indotyphlops-braminus.text: Carried around the world in plant pots; it has established populations in Florida and Hawaii.

zamenis-scalaris.text: Arrived in the Pityusic Islands with imported ornamental olive trees (first seen on Formentera in 2006); the introduced snakes are blamed for the decline of the endemic Ibiza wall lizard.

src.title: Goodbye to innocence - the silent death and disappearing of the Ibiza wall lizard Podarcis pityusensis caused by introduced snakes
src.authors: M. van den Berg & M. Zawadzki

hemorrhois-hippocrepis.text: Arrived with imported olive trees (first seen on Ibiza in 2003); on Ibiza it feeds mainly on the endemic Ibiza wall lizard, which is declining fast where the snake has spread.

src.title: Ibiza wall lizard devastated by invasive snake (on Montes et al., Current Zoology)

hemorrhois-hippocrepis.text: The Italian snakes share their genes with snakes from Tunisia and eastern Algeria, so they were most likely brought from North Africa by people.

src.title: Phylogenetic relationships of the Italian populations of Horseshoe Whip Snake Hemorrhois hippocrepis

macroprotodon-mauritanicus.text: Probably brought from North Africa in antiquity (possibly Roman times); long-established on Mallorca and Menorca.

src.title: La serp de garriga balear
src.publisher: Enciclopèdia Catalana: Història Natural dels Països Catalans

natrix-maura.text: Brought to Mallorca and Menorca by people; genetic work points to an origin in south-eastern France around Roman times. On Mallorca it preys on the rare Mallorcan midwife toad.

src.title: Introduced alien or persecuted native? Resolving the origin of the viperine snake (Natrix maura) on Mallorca
